task.title: Invoke one validated extension tool through the developer CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/647 by connecting one explicit JSON request to the isolated Wasm tool and caller-owned permission boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Parse exactly one JSON input value before extension filesystem access and select exactly one validated tool ID fail-closed.
Activate only that tool with default limits in a fresh registry and authorize only its Pure effect for one invocation.
Print one compact JSON value on success and no partial stdout with one escaped diagnostic for scoped failures.
Document that the command grants no persistence, reusable permission, retry, host import, watching, or skill and workflow execution.

attempts.summary: Established RED coverage for exact JSON invocation and fail-closed inputs.
attempts.diagnostic: The CLI integration test failed because invoke was not a recognized extension subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added command-level coverage for a generated echo component, malformed input before root access, wrong-kind selection, and invalid component activation.

attempts.summary: Implemented one-shot orchestration through existing extension and kernel contracts.
attempts.diagnostic: A fresh registry plus an authorizer scoped to one exact ID, one Pure effect, and one call kept explicit developer intent narrower than a reusable activation or grant.
attempts.patch: Parsed input first, discovered and selected one tool, activated it with default limits, invoked it through ToolRegistry authorization, and emitted compact JSON or a shared escaped diagnostic.

attempts.summary: Reconciled the documented failure contract after substantive review.
attempts.diagnostic: The detailed extension documentation omitted malformed INPUT_JSON from its no-partial-stdout guarantee while the README used the overbroad phrase every failure.
attempts.patch: Updated both documentation sites to enumerate malformed input and the scoped discovery, selection, activation, authorization, guest, trap, resource-limit, and malformed-output failure classes.

outcome.summary: The developer CLI now invokes one exact validated no-import Wasm tool with one JSON value through fresh resource limits and a non-reusable caller-owned permission decision.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30244099741 and substantive exact-head CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/648

lessons: An explicit CLI request can own a narrow permission decision without turning selected metadata or process-local activation into ambient authority.
Parsing input before filesystem access makes malformed requests fail earlier and keeps failure ordering deterministic.
Fresh registries, adapters, stores, and one-use authorization make the command an invocation boundary rather than an enablement lifecycle.

The substantive review found that detailed documentation omitted malformed INPUT_JSON from the no-partial-stdout guarantee; both documentation sites were updated to enumerate malformed input and the scoped invocation failure classes.
Failure guarantees should enumerate their intended classes so documentation neither omits required cases nor promises behavior outside the defined boundary.
